task_33.title: Prevent empty builds from unrelated parent Git ignore rules
task_33.description: Adjust packaging-time Git detection so a build started from a directory that is itself ignored by an enclosing repository does not inherit ignore rules from that unrelated parent tree. This prevents Poetry-generated artifacts from excluding the whole project and ending up empty.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that building a package does not treat ignore rules from an unrelated parent Git repository as project exclusions when the project directory itself is under a Git-ignored path, so generated artifacts are not empty.

expectation.grounded: When poetry-core resolves VCS state for packaging, `poetry.core.vcs.get_vcs` should return no Git repository for a directory that Git reports as ignored, instead of resolving a parent repository with top-level discovery. Builders that derive excluded files from VCS ignore rules must therefore avoid applying ignored-file lists from an unrelated parent work tree to the package being built.
expectation.conceptual: Package builds should only use Git ignore information from the actual tracked project repository. If the build is launched from a directory inside an ignored path of some other repository, Poetry should behave as though no repository is associated for exclusion purposes.

constraints.grounded: Do not change normal exclusion behavior for projects that are genuinely inside a valid Git work tree and are not themselves ignored. Explicit package include and exclude settings must remain authoritative, and inability to detect Git must continue to fall back to non-VCS packaging behavior rather than introducing a new error.
constraints.conceptual: Keep existing build behavior unchanged for normal Git-backed projects, preserve explicit packaging rules, and handle non-repository cases safely without introducing new build failures.

behavior: A directory that Git marks as ignored is no longer treated as belonging to an enclosing repository for packaging exclusion logic.
When no applicable Git repository is associated with the build directory, VCS-derived ignored files are treated as empty instead of being inherited from a parent repository.
Builds launched from nested directories under ignored parent paths no longer exclude the entire project because of an unrelated parent `.gitignore`.
Generated artifacts include the project's intended files instead of becoming empty solely due to bogus parent Git root detection.
acceptance_criteria: When a project is built from a directory that lies under a parent repository's ignored path, the build should not use that parent repository's `.gitignore` to determine excluded files.
When such a build generates a wheel, it should contain the project's package contents rather than an empty payload caused by inherited parent ignore rules.

When the project directory is inside a normal tracked Git repository and is not itself ignored, VCS-based ignore handling should continue to exclude files according to that repository's standard Git ignore configuration.
When Git repository detection is unavailable or intentionally skipped for the current directory, packaging should continue without VCS-derived exclusions and without a new user-visible error.

task_34.title: Correct exported markers for dependencies pulled in by extras
task_34.description: Updates export behavior so dependencies introduced through selected extras are emitted with correct markers. Transitive packages required by an enabled extra no longer keep stale extra-based conditions in the exported output, while valid platform and Python-version conditions are preserved.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that exported dependency files generate correct markers for packages required by a selected extra, so transitive dependencies are exported as actual resolved requirements instead of remaining incorrectly gated by extra-specific conditions.

expectation.grounded: When `poetry export` walks dependencies for a requirement declared with extras such as `package[extra]`, the propagated marker used for downstream packages must remove `extra == ...` constraints after combining markers. Exported entries for transitive dependencies discovered through that extra should therefore omit extra-based markers, while still preserving applicable non-extra markers such as Python-version or platform conditions.
expectation.conceptual: Selecting an extra should make all packages required by that extra appear in the exported dependency output as normal resolved dependencies. The export may still include ordinary environment conditions, but it should not continue to treat those packages as conditional on the extra after that extra has already been chosen.

constraints.grounded: Do not change dependency inclusion semantics for graphs that do not rely on extras. Do not drop legitimate non-extra marker conditions during export. Do not emit stale `extra` marker clauses on already-selected transitive dependencies in generated requirement or constraint output.
constraints.conceptual: Keep existing export behavior intact outside this bug fix. Preserve real environment-specific conditions, and only remove leftover extra gating that no longer reflects the resolved dependency set.

behavior: `poetry export` strips extra-specific marker clauses from the combined marker state once a dependency introduced by a selected extra is accepted during dependency walking.
A transitive dependency that is required because an extra was selected is exported as a concrete resolved dependency entry rather than remaining conditional on that extra marker.
If that same transitive dependency is also subject to non-extra conditions such as platform or Python version, those conditions remain represented in the exported marker.
Exported dependency files no longer carry stale extra-marker fragments on downstream packages reached through extra-enabled dependencies.
acceptance_criteria: When exporting dependencies for a project that includes a requirement with extras, any transitive package required because of the selected extra should appear in the exported output without an `extra == ...` condition.
When such a transitive package also has a valid platform or Python-version condition, the exported output should retain that condition while omitting the extra condition.
When the same package is reached through both an enabled extra and another dependency edge, the exported output should reflect the resolved package requirement without stale extra-based gating.
When exporting dependency graphs that do not depend on extras, marker generation should remain unchanged.
